Hi Maya — thanks for the forecast and the deadline callout. Short answer: yes, we have a couple of practical paths. Outline below so procurement can pick which they prefer: 

Option A — Amortized top-up + capped true-up (recommended)- Redwood invoices the uplift split evenly across the remaining invoice periods in Q3 (so you get no single-month shock).- We set a soft cap on monthly billable tokens for the pilot (based on your forecast + 20% buffer). Any usage above cap is recorded for true-up but not invoiced during the pilot; true-up occurs at the end of the pilot and can be converted to credits if you commit to the renewed term.- If you convert into renewal commitment within 30 days of pilot end, we offer a retroactive pilot discount of 8% applied to billed uplift and a 6% on the converted committed volume for the first renewal year.

Option B — Temporary voucher + standard billing- Issue an interim voucher (prepaid credit) sized to expected uplift and consume as usage happens; invoices continue as normal and voucher auto-applies. Lower operational complexity but requires up-front spend approval from finance.

High-level numbers from a quick calc (based on your sheet): uplift ~ $48k over 6 weeks. Amortized over 2 remaining invoices => ~$24k added to each invoice vs single $48k spike. With the recommended retroactive discount (opt-in on renewal), net pilot cost ~ $44k. 

I'll loop Ben on margin/discount floor and Soojin for legal/contract path for a short-term amendment. If either of those options works, I'll prepare an amendment draft today.

Would you prefer Option A or B? If Option A, do you want our suggested soft cap (+20%) or a tighter +10%?

Best,
Priyom
